summary: This Wikipedia article on San Diego covers the city's arts and performance venues, its demographics and population figures from 2000 to 2014, and its border with Mexico and transborder metropolitan area. It also summarizes the wireless and software industry presence, the city's Spanish colonial founding with Fort Presidio and Mission San Diego de Alcalá, and its incorporation and charter history. The note ends with early European exploration of the bay by Cabrillo and Vizcaíno.
one_line: Wikipedia overview of San Diego, California, covering its arts venues, population, Mexico border, industry, Spanish founding, and early exploration.
key_facts: The San Diego Symphony at Symphony Towers is directed by Jahja Ling.
The San Diego Opera at Civic Center Plaza, directed by Ian Campbell, was ranked by Opera America as one of the top 10 opera companies in the United States.
The La Jolla Playhouse at UCSD is directed by Christopher Ashley.
The Joan B. Kroc Theatre at Kroc Center's Performing Arts Center is a 600-seat theatre.
The city of San Diego had a population of 1,307,402 according to the 2010 census, over a land area of 372.1 square miles.
San Diego hosts the busiest international border crossing in the world, at the San Ysidro Port of Entry.
Qualcomm was founded and is headquartered in San Diego and is one of the largest private-sector employers in the city.
In May 1769, Gaspar de Portolà established the Fort Presidio of San Diego on a hill near the San Diego River.
In July 1769, Mission San Diego de Alcalá was founded by Franciscan friars under Junípero Serra.
With an estimated population of 1,381,069 as of July 1, 2014, San Diego is the eighth-largest city in the United States and second-largest in California.
The state of California was admitted to the United States in 1850, the same year San Diego was designated the seat of the newly established San Diego County and was incorporated as a city.
Joshua H. Bean, the last alcalde of San Diego, was elected the first mayor.
Two years after incorporation the city was bankrupt, and the California legislature revoked its charter until 1889.
Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo claimed the bay for the Spanish Empire in 1542 and named the site 'San Miguel'.
On November 12, 1602, the first Christian religious service of record in Alta California was conducted by Friar Antonio de la Ascensión to celebrate the feast day of San Diego.
